transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi. I'm here because... honestly, I just can't keep living like this. I spend pretty much my entire day, I mean from the moment I wake up until I just finally collapse, going back over the exact same things in my house. It's the electrical outlets, the locks on the doors, my tools in the garage, even just the dust on the shelves and the baseboards. 

Like, with the outlets, I have to check them, but then I walk into the next room and immediately think, wait, did I actually look at the bottom socket, or did I just look at the top one? So I have to go back. And the locks... I’ll push the deadbolt in, but then I have to jiggle the handle, and if it doesn't feel exactly right, I have to unlock it and do it all over again. And my tools, I'm constantly fixing how they're laid out, checking the dust around them, wiping things down because if it's not right, I just can't move on to the next thing. 

It's just this endless loop. I check and fix them, over and over and over again. And I get so physically worn out from all the pacing and the checking, my legs ache and I'm just completely exhausted, but no matter how many times I stare right at the lock or the outlet, I still don't feel sure enough to just walk away and leave it alone. I just never feel sure. So I stay stuck there doing it for hours, and it takes up my whole day, every single day.
Do you find yourself having persistent, unwanted thoughts or images that pop into your mind, especially when you're doing these checks or feeling the need to fix things just right?

Yeah, it's exactly like that. It's... it's these pictures, these really ugly thoughts that just force their way in, and I can't stop them. Like, I used to do some handyman work, you know, just odd jobs here and there before I stopped working, so I know how to handle tools and I know how outlets work. I *know* I did the job right. I can look right at the wall and know it's fine. But then, out of nowhere, my brain just goes, "What if there's a loose wire behind that plate?" And it's not just a passing thought, it's this vivid, terrifying image of a spark, and the drywall catching fire, and the whole house just burning to the ground in the middle of the night. 

Or with the tools in the garage... I'll put everything away, I'll sweep up the floor, but then this thought just jumps into my head that I dropped a nail somewhere. And I see my wife walking out there in her sandals to get something from the chest freezer, and she steps on it, and it goes right into her foot and she gets hurt, all because I was careless. I try so hard to just shake my head and push those thoughts out. I'll literally say out loud to myself, "You swept the floor, it's fine," or "You checked the wire, it's safe." I really, really try to just block it out and go inside and sit on the couch. But the harder I try to push them away, they just... they come right back, and they're even stronger. They get so loud in my head, like they're screaming at me that I'm being irresponsible and my wife is going to get hurt if I don't go back and check. So I just have to go back. I can't just sit there with that thought in my head, you know? I have to go make sure.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including persistent unwanted thoughts (intrusive images of harm), repetitive behaviors (checking outlets, locks, tools), and the compulsion to neutralize the distressing thoughts through checking behaviors, are most consistent with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, specifically with predominantly obsessional thoughts (F42.2). Other subtypes (e.g., F42.0, F42.1) are less consistent with the described presentation.
